name: OpenAI Image Edit
description: OpenAI image edit/extend — create an edited or extended image from a source image and a prompt (gpt-image-1 / dall-e-2).

prompt.description: Text description of the desired edit.

image.description: Source image as a file upload (_file object with data, filename, contentType).

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.orth.sh/openai/images/edits with JSON body {prompt, model, images:[{data,filename,contentType}]} — x402 paid, ~$0.08

inputExample.prompt: add a small red circle in the center

usage.outputShape: body.data[].b64_json (or body.data[].url) on success — OpenAI image-edit response shape { created, data: [...] }; errors at body.error.{message,type,param,code}
quirks: Registry/discovery inputSchema is WRONG: it lists a single 'image' string field. OpenAI rejects that: 'Unknown parameter: image. For application/json on /v1/images/edits, use images (array).'

The correct field is 'images' and it must be an ARRAY of FILE OBJECTS, not strings. A base64/data-URL string is rejected: 'Invalid type for images[0]: expected an object, but got a string instead.' Use images:[{data,filename,contentType}] (the _file object convention).

This is a thin passthrough proxy to OpenAI POST /v1/images/edits — body is forwarded as application/json. All validation errors come straight from OpenAI, so OpenAI's images.edits JSON-mode schema is the source of truth.
Payment is real and confirms on Base (got txHashes); a 400 still charges $0.08 because the proxy pays-then-forwards. Get the body shape right BEFORE paying.
'prompt' is required; 'model' (gpt-image-1 or dall-e-2), n, size, quality, user are optional.

QA stopped at 2 paid attempts ($0.16) per money-safety ceiling without landing a 2xx; the images:[{data,filename,contentType}] shape is inferred from the OpenAI error chain and should be confirmed on first live use.
usage.guide: POST https://x402.orth.sh/openai/images/edits as JSON with x402 payment (~$0.08/call on Base, no API key). Send {prompt, model, images:[{data, filename, contentType}]} where each images[] entry is a file object: data = base64 of the source image bytes, filename e.g. 'src.png', contentType e.g. 'image/png'. Do NOT use the 'image' field or a bare base64 string — both are rejected with HTTP 400 (and you still get charged). On success read the edited image from body.data[].b64_json (or body.data[].url). It is a passthrough to OpenAI /v1/images/edits, so OpenAI's image-edit JSON contract applies.

name: AI Image Upscaler
description: Upscale / super-resolution — increase image resolution with AI.

usage.outputShape: No successful output produced. On failure: body.error (string). A working response is undocumented; both paid calls returned only an error object.
quirks: Charge-then-fail: charges $0.10 USDC even when upscaling fails. First paid call with a valid public image_url returned 502 {error:'Upscaling failed: Unprocessable Entity'}.
Required body field is image_url (a URL string). Using 'image' instead returns 400 {error:"Missing 'image_url' field"}.
Could not obtain a single successful upscale across 2 paid attempts ($0.20 spent). Upstream model appears to reject otherwise-valid images.
txHash not captured / confirmed:false on both paid calls.
usage.guide: Call POST https://x402-deployer.x402-deployer.workers.dev/upscale-image with JSON body {"image_url":"<public image URL>"} and pay $0.10 USDC via x402 on Base. The required field is image_url (omitting it returns 400 'Missing image_url field'). WARNING: this endpoint is currently broken — it charges $0.10 even on failure, and in QA it returned 502 'Upscaling failed: Unprocessable Entity' for a valid public image. Avoid until upstream is fixed; the working output shape is unknown.

name: Image Outpainting (Expand)
description: Bria Image Expand — outpaint / extend an image beyond its original borders.

usage.callShape: POST https://x402-deployer.x402-deployer.workers.dev/image-expand with JSON body {image_url, canvas_width, canvas_height, original_image_width, original_image_height, x_offset, y_offset}
usage.outputShape: unknown — no successful response captured. On error: body.error (string). Expected success likely body.result / image url/base64 (Bria Image Expand), but unverified.
quirks: No inputSchema in registry; body shape discovered by probing. Uses FLAT snake_case params, NOT arrays: canvas_width, canvas_height, original_image_width, original_image_height, x_offset, y_offset.
canvas_width must be a number between 256 and 4096 (same constraint presumably for canvas_height).
Sending canvas_size/original_image_size/original_image_location as arrays returns 400 'canvas_width must be a number between 256 and 4096'.

Even with correctly-named flat params the upstream Bria call returned 502 'Image expand failed: Unprocessable Entity' (422 from upstream) — geometry/values rejected or upstream unstable. PAID but no usable output in 2 attempts ($0.30 total lost).
Endpoint charges $0.15 per call and is non-refundable on upstream error — validate geometry carefully before paying.
usage.guide: POST to https://x402-deployer.x402-deployer.workers.dev/image-expand (x402, $0.15 on Base, no auth). Send JSON with image_url plus FLAT snake_case geometry: canvas_width, canvas_height (each 256-4096), original_image_width, original_image_height, and x_offset/y_offset positioning the original inside the canvas. Do NOT use array forms like canvas_size. In QA the deployer accepted the flat shape but upstream Bria returned 502 'Unprocessable Entity', so no successful expansion was produced — treat output as unverified and ensure the original fully fits within the canvas (offset + original dimension <= canvas dimension) before paying, since each call costs real USDC and errors are not refunded.

usage.outputShape: body.enhanced_image_url (the upscaled/enhanced PNG URL); body.changes_applied[] (list of enhancements), body.quality_score (number), body.processedAt
usage.guide: Send a POST to https://gg402.vercel.app/image_enhancer with a JSON body containing the field image_url pointing to a public image URL. Pay the $0.010 USDC x402 charge on Base. The response is synchronous JSON; read the enhanced result from body.enhanced_image_url and inspect body.changes_applied[] and body.quality_score for what was done. No auth, no polling, no templates.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/image-resize?image_url=<URL>&target_width=<int>&target_height=<int>&format=png&fit=cover (all params are query string; all optional but image_url + target dims needed for a useful result)
usage.outputShape: body.base64 (resized image, base64-encoded), body.width, body.height, body.format, body.size_bytes, body.content_type; metadata at body._meta.payment
quirks: All inputs are QUERY-STRING params on a GET (no JSON body): image_url, target_width, target_height, format (png|jpeg|webp), fit (cover|contain|fill|inside|outside), quality.
URL-encode image_url.

CHARGES EVEN ON FAILURE: a source image the server cannot fetch returns HTTP 400 'Failed to fetch image' but STILL bills ~$0.0324. Use a reliably server-fetchable image URL (a Wikipedia upload.wikimedia.org URL was rejected with 400; httpbin.org/image/png worked).
Output image is returned as base64 string in body.base64, not a binary body.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.strale.io/x402/image-resize with query params: image_url (URL-encoded, must be a publicly+server-fetchable image), target_width, target_height, plus optional format (png/jpeg/webp) and fit (cover/contain/fill/inside/outside). It pays via x402 (~$0.032/call on Base) and returns JSON synchronously. Read the resized image from body.base64 (decode it), with body.width/height/format/size_bytes describing the result. Important: pick an image URL you know the server can fetch — bad/blocked URLs return HTTP 400 but you are still charged.

name: Image Metadata Scrubber
description: Strip EXIF/XMP metadata from an image for privacy.

usage.callShape: POST https://utilsforagents.com/v1/image/scrub-metadata — body MUST be raw binary image bytes with Content-Type: image/jpeg or image/png, OR multipart/form-data with field 'file' = the image binary (max 5 MB). NOT JSON, NOT base64.

inputExample._note: no JSON body — send raw image bytes with Content-Type: image/png, or multipart/form-data field 'file' = <binary JPEG/PNG>

usage.outputShape: Response body is the raw cleaned image binary (Content-Type matches the uploaded image format, image/jpeg or image/png) with all EXIF/XMP/IPTC metadata stripped. There is no JSON wrapper — save the response bytes directly as the output image file.
quirks: Binary upload endpoint: requires raw image bytes (Content-Type: image/jpeg|image/png) OR multipart/form-data with field 'file'. Does NOT accept a JSON body or a base64 string.
Output is raw binary image bytes (no JSON envelope); response Content-Type matches the original image format. Save the bytes directly.
Max image size 5 MB.

COULD NOT TEST via the qa-pay harness: that tool only sends Content-Type application/json, reads --body=@file as utf8 text (corrupting binary), and has no multipart/octet-stream support — so it cannot deliver a valid image to this endpoint. Did not pay (paying would charge $0.003 then 4xx with no usable result). Needs an x402 client that can POST raw binary / multipart file bodies to verify.
Decoded payment-required (x402 v2) confirms input bodyType 'form-data' with required field 'file' and output type 'binary'.
usage.guide: POST the image to https://utilsforagents.com/v1/image/scrub-metadata to strip EXIF/XMP/IPTC metadata. Send the image either as a raw binary body with Content-Type set to image/jpeg or image/png, or as multipart/form-data with a single field named 'file' containing the image bytes (max 5 MB). Pay the $0.003 USDC x402 charge (Base eip155:8453 or Solana). The response body is the cleaned image as raw binary bytes (no JSON) with Content-Type matching the original format — write those bytes straight to a file. Do NOT send a JSON or base64 body; it will be rejected. NOTE: this endpoint was not paid-tested because the QA pay harness cannot send binary/multipart bodies — verify with a binary-capable x402 client before trusting.

name: Image to SVG (vectorize)
description: Convert an existing raster image (PNG/JPG/etc.) into a vector SVG. StableStudio's arrow model family. Two quality tiers as interchangeable backends: arrow-1.1 (default, $0.15, ~30s) and arrow-1.1-max ($0.20, ~60s, higher fidelity). Same input/output for both. Requires the image to be uploaded via StableStudio's blob-upload flow first; the operation is async (pay -> jobId -> poll for SVG).

usage.callShape: PREREQUISITE 3-step upload flow (the `image` MUST be a Vercel Blob URL from THIS flow; external URLs are rejected): (1) POST https://stablestudio.dev/api/upload (x402, $0.01) with {filename, contentType:'image/png', size?} -> {uploadId, clientToken, pathname, expiresAt, curlExample}. (2) PUT raw image bytes to https://vercel.com/api/blob/?pathname=<urlencoded pathname> with headers authorization:'Bearer <clientToken>', x-content-type:'image/png', x-api-version:'11' (free) -> {url}. (3) POST https://stablestudio.dev/api/upload/confirm (SIWX, free) with {uploadId, blobUrl:<that url>} -> {success, upload:{blobUrl}}. THEN the vectorize op: POST https://stablestudio.dev/api/generate/arrow-1.1/vectorize (x402, $0.15) with JSON {image:<blobUrl>, target_size:1024, auto_crop:false} -> {success:true, jobId, status:'pending', type:'arrow-1.1-vectorize'}. THEN poll GET https://stablestudio.dev/api/jobs/{jobId} (SIGN-IN-WITH-X, free, signed by the SAME wallet that paid) every ~5s until status='complete'.
usage.outputShape: POST vectorize: success(bool), jobId(str), status('pending'), type(str). Poll GET /api/jobs/{jobId}: id, type, input{...}, status('loading'|'complete'|'failed'), progress(0-100), result.imageUrl (an .svg blob URL on complete), error(null|str), createdAt, updatedAt. Final SVG = result.imageUrl.
quirks: FIELD-NAME / not-self-contained trap: the `image` field is documented in OpenAPI as just 'Image URL to vectorize' but in practice it MUST be a Vercel Blob URL produced by StableStudio's own upload flow. You CANNOT pass an arbitrary external image URL.
Upload flow is a hard prerequisite and costs an EXTRA $0.01 (POST /api/upload) on top of the vectorize price. Total to get one SVG = $0.16 (arrow-1.1) or $0.21 (arrow-1.1-max).
Upload Step 2 PUT goes to vercel.com (vercel_blob client token), NOT to stablestudio.dev. Headers x-content-type and x-api-version:11 are required.

Two-step async: the paid POST only returns {jobId, status:'pending'}; the actual SVG comes from polling GET /api/jobs/{jobId} which is SIGN-IN-WITH-X auth (free) and MUST be signed by the same wallet that paid.
Job status sequence observed: pending -> loading(progress:10) -> complete(progress:100). Completed in ~13s for arrow-1.1. Poll every ~5s. arrow-1.1-max ~60s.
result.imageUrl is an .svg blob URL that expires ~20 min after completion - download immediately.

Optional body fields (defaults): target_size 1024 (128-4096), auto_crop false, prompt '' (ignored for vectorize), max_output_tokens 4096, temperature 1, top_p 1, presence_penalty 0. Only `image` is required.
Pays USDC on Base (x402; mpp also supported), no API key.
arrow-1.1 vs arrow-1.1-max are the SAME operation with identical input/output schema - only price/latency/fidelity differ; treat as interchangeable backends, not separate services.
usage.guide: Convert an existing raster image (PNG/JPG/etc.) into a vector SVG. StableStudio's arrow model family. Two quality tiers as interchangeable backends: arrow-1.1 (default, $0.15, ~30s) and arrow-1.1-max ($0.20, ~60s, higher fidelity). Same input/output for both. Requires the image to be uploaded via StableStudio's blob-upload flow first; the operation is async (pay -> jobId -> poll for SVG). PREREQUISITE 3-step upload flow (the `image` MUST be a Vercel Blob URL from THIS flow; external URLs are rejected): (1) POST https://stablestudio.dev/api/upload (x402, $0.01) with {filename, contentType:'image/png', size?} -> {uploadId, clientToken, pathname, expiresAt, curlExample}. (2) PUT raw image bytes to https://vercel.com/api/blob/?pathname=<urlencoded pathname> with headers authorization:'Bearer <clientToken>', x-content-type:'image/png', x-api-version:'11' (free) -> {url}. (3) POST https://stablestudio.dev/api/upload/confirm (SIWX, free) with {uploadId, blobUrl:<that url>} -> {success, upload:{blobUrl}}. THEN the vectorize op: POST https://stablestudio.dev/api/generate/arrow-1.1/vectorize (x402, $0.15) with JSON {image:<blobUrl>, target_size:1024, auto_crop:false} -> {success:true, jobId, status:'pending', type:'arrow-1.1-vectorize'}. THEN poll GET https://stablestudio.dev/api/jobs/{jobId} (SIGN-IN-WITH-X, free, signed by the SAME wallet that paid) every ~5s until status='complete'. Output: POST vectorize: success(bool), jobId(str), status('pending'), type(str). Poll GET /api/jobs/{jobId}: id, type, input{...}, status('loading'|'complete'|'failed'), progress(0-100), result.imageUrl (an .svg blob URL on complete), error(null|str), createdAt, updatedAt. Final SVG = result.imageUrl.

name: Image-to-Image Edit
description: Edit or vary an existing image with a text prompt. Send the source image (and optional mask) as a base64 data URI. OpenAI gpt-image-1 / gpt-image-2 support mask-based inpainting; Google nano-banana / nano-banana-pro do prompt-only edits (mask not supported).

usage.callShape: POST https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/images/image2image with body {prompt, image} (image = base64 data URI; optional model, mask, size, n) -> returns OpenAI-style {created, data[]} with the edited image(s) synchronously.

inputExample.prompt: make the sky a vivid sunset orange

quirks: Dynamic pricing $0.02-$0.16 per call depending on model/size/n; min $0.02. Live default 402 (minimal body) quoted $0.063 (pricePerImage $0.06, gpt-image-1, 1024x1024, n=1).
image must be a base64 data URI (e.g. data:image/png;base64,...), not a URL.
mask-based inpainting only supported by openai/gpt-image-1 and gpt-image-2; google/nano-banana + nano-banana-pro do prompt-only edits (mask ignored/unsupported).
Cost scales with n (number of images) -> charge multiplies; keep n=1 for cheapest test.
x402 v2: USDC on Base (eip155:8453). Accepts present in payment-required / x-payment-required / www-authenticate headers AND JSON body.
Charge-then-error risk possible since it proxies upstream model providers (OpenAI/Google); pay-test with a tiny valid image and short prompt.

name: 24kLabs Blur Image
description: Apply a Gaussian blur at a given radius to an image (useful for redaction backdrops), via a pay-per-call x402 endpoint.

image_b64.description: Source image as base64-encoded bytes (no data-URL prefix)

usage.callShape: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/image-blur with a JSON body {"image_b64": <base64 image bytes, no data-URL prefix>, "radius": <number>}. Pure x402 (USDC on Base, no API key). Synchronous — the blurred image is returned inline in the 200 response as base64.
usage.outputShape: body.service ("image-blur"), body.result.format (e.g. "PNG"), body.result.width/height/bytes, body.result.image_b64 (the Gaussian-blurred image as base64), body.latency_ms
quirks: Deterministic image transform (Pillow-style Gaussian blur) — no upstream LLM.
Input image is passed inline as a base64 string in image_b64 (raw bytes, NOT a data-URL and NOT a URL). The blurred result comes back the same way at result.image_b64.
radius controls blur strength; the documented example uses radius 2. Only image_b64 is strictly required (radius has a default).
Same-host namespace alias exists at /api/v1/image-blur; index only /api/image-blur.
Verified with the provider's documented 8x8 PNG example — output preserved format PNG at 8x8.
usage.guide: POST to https://api.24klabs.ai/api/image-blur with a JSON body containing the source image in 'image_b64' (base64-encoded image bytes, no data-URL prefix) and an optional 'radius' (blur strength, e.g. 2). The endpoint is x402-paid (~$0.003 USDC on Base, scheme exact) and responds synchronously with 200. Read the blurred image from result.image_b64 (base64); result.format/width/height describe it. Verified: the documented example {image_b64:<8x8 PNG>, radius:2} returned a blurred 8x8 PNG.

name: 24kLabs Crop Image
description: Crop an image to a pixel box (left, top, right, bottom) and return the cropped image.

inputSchema.left: number (left edge of crop box, pixels)
inputSchema.top: number (top edge of crop box, pixels)
inputSchema.right: number (right edge of crop box, pixels)
inputSchema.bottom: number (bottom edge of crop box, pixels)

usage.callShape: POST JSON body { image_b64, left, top, right, bottom }
usage.outputShape: json: { service, result: { format, width, height, bytes, image_b64 }, latency_ms } — result.image_b64 is the base64-encoded cropped image
usage.quirks: Single-shot synchronous crop. image_b64 is a base64 (not data-URL) image; the box is given as absolute pixel coordinates left/top/right/bottom. The /api/v1/image-crop path is the same op on the same host (a namespace alias) and must not be indexed/paid separately.
usage.guide: Send a POST with JSON { image_b64, left, top, right, bottom } where image_b64 is the base64-encoded source image and left/top/right/bottom are pixel coordinates of the crop box. Example: an 8x8 PNG with { left:0, top:0, right:4, bottom:4 } returns result.image_b64 as a 4x4 PNG (result.width==4, result.height==4). Pays x402 (USDC on Base, $0.002/call); the cropped image is inline in the 200 (no polling).

name: 24kLabs Image Dominant Color
description: Extract the dominant color palette from an image as hex/RGB codes with per-color coverage percentages, via a pay-per-call x402 endpoint.

image_b64.description: The source image encoded as a base64 string (raw base64 bytes, no data-URL prefix)

count.description: Number of dominant colors to return (default 5)

coverage_pct.description: Percent of pixels covered by this color

usage.callShape: POST JSON body { image_b64, count? } — image_b64 is the raw base64-encoded image bytes (no data-URL prefix); count optionally sets how many dominant colors to return (default 5). Result is returned inline (synchronous) in the 200 under result.palette.
usage.quirks: image_b64 must be RAW base64 (no 'data:image/png;base64,' prefix). count is optional (defaults to 5). Palette entries are ordered by coverage_pct descending. Namespace alias /api/v1/image-dominant-color is the same op on the same host (deferred).
usage.needs: An image, base64-encoded into the image_b64 field.
usage.guide: Base64-encode your image (raw bytes, no data-URL prefix) and POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/image-dominant-color with JSON body { "image_b64": "<base64>", "count": 5 }. Pays via x402 (Base USDC, $0.004). Response returns result.palette — an array of { hex, rgb, coverage_pct } dominant colors, ordered by coverage.

name: 24kLabs Image Grayscale
description: Convert an image to grayscale (or sepia/duotone).

inputSchema.image_b64: string (required) — base64 of the source image bytes, no data-URL prefix

result.image_b64: string — base64 of the grayscaled image

usage.callShape: POST JSON body { image_b64 } (base64 image bytes, no data-URL prefix)
usage.outputShape: json: { service, result: { format, width, height, bytes, image_b64 }, latency_ms } — result.image_b64 is the base64 of the grayscaled image (no data-URL prefix)
usage.quirks: Single-shot synchronous image filter. Input is base64 image bytes in image_b64 (no data:image prefix); output image is returned inline in the 200 as result.image_b64 (no polling). The 402 serviceName is 'Grayscale / Duotone' and the description mentions sepia, so an optional sepia/duotone mode param likely exists (body additionalProperties:true) but is not in the documented schema — the only documented/required field is image_b64. The /api/v1/image-grayscale path is the same op on the same host (a namespace alias) and must not be indexed/paid separately.
usage.guide: Send a POST with JSON { image_b64 } where image_b64 is the base64 of the source image bytes (no data-URL prefix). The grayscaled result comes back inline in the 200 at result.image_b64 (also base64, no prefix), along with result.{format,width,height,bytes}. Pays x402 (USDC on Base, $0.002/call); synchronous, no polling. Verified live with the provider's tiny 8x8 PNG example.

name: 24kLabs Image Metadata
description: Report the format, dimensions, mode, aspect ratio, transparency, and byte size of an image, via a pay-per-call x402 endpoint.

format.description: Detected image format, e.g. PNG, JPEG

usage.callShape: POST JSON body { image_b64 } where image_b64 is the raw base64 of the image bytes (no data: prefix); metadata is returned inline (synchronous) in the 200 under result.{format,width,height,mode,aspect_ratio,has_alpha,bytes,megapixels}.
usage.quirks: image_b64 is the raw base64 of the image bytes (NOT a data-URI, NOT a URL). Namespace alias /api/v1/image-metadata is the same op on the same host (deferred).
usage.needs: The image bytes, base64-encoded, in the image_b64 field.
usage.guide: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/image-metadata with JSON body { "image_b64": "<base64 of the image bytes>" }. Pays via x402 (Base USDC, $0.002). Response returns result with format, width, height, mode, aspect_ratio, has_alpha, bytes and megapixels inline in the 200.

name: 24kLabs Image Rotate
description: Rotate an image by a given number of degrees and/or flip it horizontally or vertically; returns the transformed PNG as base64.

image_b64.description: Source image as base64-encoded bytes (no data-URL prefix)
Rotated image as base64-encoded PNG bytes

usage.callShape: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/image-rotate with JSON body {image_b64, degrees} — image_b64 = base64 of the source image bytes (NO data-URL prefix); degrees = rotation angle. x402 paid ($0.002 USDC on Base), synchronous JSON response.
usage.outputShape: body.service (op id), body.result.{format, width, height, bytes, image_b64}, body.latency_ms — the rotated image is base64 PNG bytes at body.result.image_b64 (no data-URL prefix).
quirks: image_b64 must be raw base64 of the image bytes with NO 'data:image/png;base64,' prefix (the provider's documented example is a bare base64 PNG).
Output image is returned as base64 at body.result.image_b64 (decode it), not a binary body and not a URL.

The op also flips (serviceName is 'Rotate / Flip', description mentions horizontal/vertical flip); body accepts additional properties beyond image_b64/degrees, but only image_b64+degrees are in the documented schema. There is also a distinct /api/image-rotate-flip endpoint.
Pay-tested live 2026-07-30 with the provider's documented example body: HTTP 200, $0.002 charged (txHash not surfaced by the pay harness, confirmed:false).
24kLabs exposes the same op under two namespaces on this host: /api/image-rotate (indexed here) and /api/v1/image-rotate (duplicate alias, not indexed).
usage.guide: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/image-rotate with a JSON body {"image_b64":"<base64 of the image bytes, NO data-URL prefix>", "degrees":<angle e.g. 90>} and pay the $0.002 USDC x402 charge on Base (no API key). The response is synchronous JSON; read the rotated image from body.result.image_b64 (base64 PNG bytes — decode and save), with body.result.{format,width,height,bytes} describing it. Do not add a 'data:image/png;base64,' prefix to image_b64. This op can also flip the image; a sibling /api/image-rotate-flip exists for explicit flip. The same op is also available at /api/v1/image-rotate (identical, not separately indexed).

name: 24kLabs Square Thumbnail
description: Create a centered square thumbnail of an image at a given pixel size.

inputSchema.image_b64: string (base64-encoded source image bytes, no data-url prefix; required)
inputSchema.size: number (target square side length in pixels; e.g. 4)

result.image_b64: string (base64 of the resized thumbnail image)

usage.outputShape: json: { service, result: { format, width, height, bytes, image_b64 }, latency_ms } — result.image_b64 is the base64-encoded resized thumbnail (a square of side = requested size)
quirks: Input image is passed as base64 in image_b64 (raw base64 of the image bytes, no data:... prefix), NOT as a URL. The output thumbnail is returned base64-encoded in result.image_b64.
size is the requested square side length in pixels; the returned width == height == size.
Single-shot synchronous op — the resized image is inline in the 200 (no polling).
The /api/v1/image-thumbnail path is the same op on the same host (a namespace alias) and must not be indexed/paid separately.
usage.guide: Send a POST with JSON { image_b64, size } where image_b64 is the raw base64 of the source image bytes (no data-url prefix) and size is the target square side length in pixels. Example {"image_b64":"<base64-png>","size":4} returns result.image_b64 (base64 of a size x size square thumbnail) plus result.{format,width,height,bytes}. Pays x402 (USDC on Base, $0.003/call); the resized image is inline in the 200 (no polling). Decode result.image_b64 to get the thumbnail bytes.

name: 24kLabs Placeholder Image
description: Generate a solid-color placeholder PNG at any width/height with optional centered text (no input image needed), via a pay-per-call x402 endpoint.

text.description: Optional centered text to render on the placeholder

image_b64.description: Base64-encoded PNG of the placeholder image

usage.callShape: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/placeholder-image with a JSON body {"width": 200, "height": 100, "text": "24K"} (width/height = pixel dimensions; text = optional centered label). Pure x402 (USDC on Base, no API key). Synchronous — the base64 PNG is returned inline in the response.
usage.outputShape: JSON object {"service":"placeholder-image","result":{"format":"PNG","width":200,"height":100,"bytes":747,"image_b64":"<base64 PNG>"}}. The generated image is the base64 PNG in result.image_b64. Observed at index time on a paid 2xx.
quirks: Output is a base64-encoded PNG in result.image_b64 (not a hosted URL); decode it to get the image.
This generates an image from scratch (no input image required) — it is a solid-color placeholder utility, not an AI image-generation model.
'text' is optional; width/height default to the provider's example dimensions if omitted (documented example uses 200x100 with text '24K').
Fixed price ~$0.002 USDC on Base (scheme exact); not dynamic.
usage.guide: POST to https://api.24klabs.ai/api/placeholder-image with a JSON body containing 'width' and 'height' (pixel dimensions) and optional 'text' (centered label). The endpoint is x402-paid (~$0.002 USDC on Base, scheme exact) and responds synchronously with {"service":"placeholder-image","result":{"format":"PNG","width","height","bytes","image_b64"}}. The placeholder image is the base64 PNG in result.image_b64 — decode it to obtain the PNG. No API key needed.

name: 24kLabs QR Code Generator
description: Generate a QR code as a base64-encoded PNG from arbitrary text, a URL, WiFi credentials, or a vCard, with control over size and error-correction, via a pay-per-call x402 endpoint.

text.description: The payload to encode: plain text, a URL, WiFi credential string, or vCard.

size.description: QR module/box size controlling output resolution (documented example uses 6).

usage.callShape: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/qr-generate with a JSON body {"text": "https://24klabs.ai", "size": 6} (text = the string to encode: URL, plain text, WiFi, or vCard; size = optional QR box size). Pure x402 (USDC on Base, no API key). Synchronous — the base64 PNG QR code is returned inline in the response.
usage.outputShape: JSON object {"service":"qr-generate","result":{"format":"PNG","width":174,"height":174,"bytes":848,"image_b64":"<base64 PNG>"}}. The QR image is the base64 PNG in result.image_b64. Observed at index time on a paid 2xx.
quirks: Output is a base64-encoded PNG in result.image_b64 (not a hosted URL); decode it to get the image.
'text' accepts URLs, plain text, WiFi credential strings, and vCards per the resource description; 'size' controls output resolution (example size 6 -> 174x174 PNG).
Same-host namespace alias exists at /api/v1/qr-generate; index only /api/qr-generate.
Fixed price ~$0.003 USDC on Base (scheme exact); not dynamic.
usage.guide: POST to https://api.24klabs.ai/api/qr-generate with a JSON body containing 'text' (the string to encode — a URL, plain text, WiFi credential, or vCard) and optional 'size' (QR box size, e.g. 6). The endpoint is x402-paid (~$0.003 USDC on Base, scheme exact) and responds synchronously with {"service":"qr-generate","result":{"format":"PNG","width","height","bytes","image_b64"}}. The QR code is the base64 PNG in result.image_b64 — decode it to obtain the PNG. No API key needed.
